body.statement: Under the two-scale geometric restriction \(q<\gamma\), \(a\asymp\ell^\alpha\), \(b\asymp\ell^\beta\), \(ab\asymp\delta\), \(h\asymp\delta^{1/\gamma}\), and \(\ell\asymp\delta^{1/q}\), sparse occupancy gives \(kp_2\asymp n^2h^d\ell^d\). Thus the two exponents in Theorem 2 are bounded below by fixed positive constants when \(\delta\ge C\max\{r_{\mathrm{pair}},r_F\}\), and can be made arbitrarily large by increasing \(C\). This is a fixed-error pure-private separation guarantee, restricted to \(q<\gamma\) and \(nv\le c_0\), at the named coupled radius \(r_F=(n^2\epsilon)^{-1/D_F}\), without a nuisance-sign logarithm. For \(k=1\) and nuisance profile \(\lambda=(\lambda_1)\in\{-1,1\}\), let \(O_i=(Y_i,A_i,X_i)\), \(i\in\{1,2\}\), be independent records from \(P_{s,(\lambda_1)}\), and set \(U_i=2A_i-1\), \(V_i=2Y_i-1\), and \(Z_{12}=(U_1V_2+V_1U_2)/2\). Then the sanity reduction is \[\mathbb E_{P_{s,(\lambda_1)}^{\otimes2}}\!\left[Z_{12}\,\middle|\,X_1,X_2\in C_1\right]=4sab.\]
body.justification: The specialization makes the \(n^2\epsilon\) privacy balance explicit without importing a formula for full-class nonprivate risk.
body.gap: Kennedy et al. derive a nonprivate fuzzy-hypothesis rate, and Acharya et al. derive private mixture converses; neither constructs a private CATE test attaining this signed-family pair separation.
body.consumer: It validates the \(r_F\) branch on the legal least-favorable experiment before any global target-fiber aggregation is attempted.
